title: Late Static Binding
learning_outcomes: Explain what late static binding contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: self versus static.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. In this lesson, focus on self versus static; then compare it with inheritance-sensitive static behavior. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use late static binding when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. For late static binding, begin with self versus static. Also distinguish inheritance-sensitive static behavior; static return types; factory methods and inherited apis. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
